page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Computer crisis
title: Computer crisis
topic: Language to use in dealing with IT (information technology) problems
description:
Disaster strikes the computers of Tip Top Trading! Something has happened and everyone's work has disappeared. Anna calls in the IT support, but can she explain to them what the problem is and can they actually help?
This episode focuses on language that you might use when sorting out a problem with your computer.
phrases: I am having problems with my computer.
I seem to have lost some documents.
I have turned the computer off and on but that hasn't fixed it.

listening_challenge.question: What is the technical term for turning the computer off and on again?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's frozen. Nothing will work…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah and all my football scores… I mean company accounts… have disappeared.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Can anyone get their computers to work? Or is just me?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to the offices of Tip Top Trading where, as you can hear, there appears to be a bit of computer trouble. Everyone's work seems to have disappeared. This is serious so who can sort it out?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Leave it to me. I'll sort it out. You just need to switch it off… and on again … like that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hold on, let's check… Denise! All my documents have gone now!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh, sorry, I was just trying to help. You'll just have to call I.T. Support, look, here’s their number.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: 'It' Support?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No Anna not 'it' but I.T. Support – information technology – sometimes called Computer Support. Most big companies have them. These are the people who sort out your computer problems and get everything working again. But be careful, they might ask some tricky questions.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, thanks. But what should I say to them?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tell them: "I am having problems with my computer", then say "the screen keeps freezing" and "I seem to have lost some documents". Tell them "I have turned the computer off and on but that hasn't fixed it". Finally, ask if they can help – please!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I'll give it a try. Here goes.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: I.T., Dave speaking, how can I help?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hello Dave – I'm having some computer problems – in fact everyone is here.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Right. What system are you using?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What system?

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Yeah, what are you using? PC, laptop, Windows XP?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Tell him it's Windows 7.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Erm… it's Windows 7 on a PC.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Good, good, this should be easy. Were you using many applications when it crashed?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Applications?

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Did you have lots of things open – documents, spreadsheets, videos, other software?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I suppose I did.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Right, well… Anna isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Right, well Anna, try pressing control, alt, delete, at the same time – after that try opening Windows again.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK. Tom, could you open the windows please.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What eh? The windows?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. Dave says so.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: No, no, no. Open Windows 7 on your computer.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, silly me! No, the screen just freezes. I'm a bit worried because I think I've lost some documents.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Hmmm. In that case the only thing to do is reboot it.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Reboot it?You mean kick it?!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No! Reboot means turn it on and off again.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh I see. No Dave, I have already tried turning it off and on again but that hasn't fixed it. What am I going to do?

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Don't panic! I'll come and have a look. You're on the 2nd floor right?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear. This is a bit worrying but I'm sure Dave, the IT man, will get things sorted. Remember if you have important documents, it's best to back them up on a memory stick just in case you have a problem like this.  Let's remind ourselves of the phrases we might use if we have to call computer support:
I am having problems with my computer
The screen keeps freezing
I seem to have lost some documents
I have turned the computer off and on but that hasn't fixed it
Can you help, please?

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Oh hi. Is Anna here?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: She's over there.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: So Anna, I'm just going to unplug the screen and put the wire back in here…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK Tom but are you OK down there? Mind your head.

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Excuse me, are you Anna? I've come to fix your computer.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, hello… you must be… Dave. I really like your hair.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ow!

transcript.speaker: I.T. Man
transcript.text: Thanks. You look rather lovely. I'd better take a look at your computer.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Don't worry guys, it’s OK, I think I've fixed it!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Looks like Tom has a rival. Is Anna going to fall for the charms of Dave, the I.T. man, or is he just going to upgrade her software? This could get very interesting – but there's still work to be done – so join us again soon for English at Work. Bye.
